title: Coefficient four with combined affine-control witnesses and explicit unscored reductions

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total family F_n defined in proof.md: F_n=0 for n<1024. For n>=1024 let k be the least prime with k^5>32*n^3, m=n-k, r=ceil(m/k), and t=ceil(sqrt(r)). The first k input bits encode the coefficients below the leading term of a monic degree-k binary polynomial q. Output 0 if q is reducible. Otherwise form K=F_2[Z]/(q), pad the remaining m input bits with zeros to r*k bits, and interpret the blocks z_i in the polynomial basis, constant coefficient first. Set y_i=z_i^(2^(r+2-i)-1) and output Tr_(K/F_2)(sum over t-element I subset {1,...,r} of product_(i in I) y_i). The field description is part of the actual n-bit input. The fixed evaluator and empty-witness NP verifier are specified in proof.md.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"For this one fixed total uniform polynomial-time Boolean family, hence one language in NP with witness bound zero, C_B2(F_n)>=4*(n-k)-9*(d(n)+1)>=4*n-(627/4)*n^(4/5) for every integer n>=1024, where d(n)=ceil(k*r/t)+k*t+r*(r+1)+1. Therefore liminf over all integer lengths n of C_B2(F_n)/n >= 4 in the full Li-Yang B2 model at actual input length n=|x|. Equivalently, for every real epsilon>0 there exists N_epsilon such that every integer n>=N_epsilon satisfies C_B2(F_n)>=(4-epsilon)*n.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}

claims: Unscored Theorem A (proof.md Section 9.2). Let d be a nonnegative integer. Let a full-cube fair affine-prefix representation on N independent coordinates, with a square invertible auxiliary matrix, rows of at most three actual terms, and an acyclic ordinary full-B2 circuit, compute a function nonconstant on every affine subspace of dimension at least d. Count every row and ordinary gate in S; computational degree of an actual parameter or auxiliary label counts distinct incident row/gate objects, with repeated pins counted once and the output reference excluded. If S<25N/6 and N>100(d+1), and J_5 counts actual labels of degree at least five, then J_5<=11*(S-4N+9*(d+1)). Arbitrary ordinary sharing and later affine uses are allowed.

Unscored Theorem B (proof.md Section 9.3). In the full-cube fair representation of Theorem A, additionally require every retained ordinary gate to have a path to the designated output. Ordinary fanout counts distinct ordinary children. Suppose S<25N/6 and N>100(d+1). Let J count the union of (i) actual affine labels of degree at least five, (ii) semantically constant actual labels of positive degree at most four, and (iii) nonconstant actual labels of degree j in {1,2,3,4} with an AND-type ordinary child having fanout at least 5-j. An AND-type table is (U+alpha)*(V+beta)+epsilon over F_2, and its other parent may be nonlinear. Then J<=16*(S-4N+9*(d+1)). This is one combined population bound, with each actual label counted once; it asserts no positive-density coverage of all circuits.

Unscored Theorem C (proof.md Section 9.4). In a full-cube fair affine-prefix representation of a d-affine disperser as defined in Theorem A, let K_0 count distinct nondegenerate bottom products P, none supplying the designated output, with actual affine parents u,v and sole ordinary child H. Suppose the other parent of H is an actual affine label L in the affine span of {1,u,v}; H may have any binary Boolean table and arbitrary sharing. Then K_0<=S-4N+9*(d+1), without the two size-range hypotheses of Theorem A. The proof performs K_0 exact two-to-one gate compositions on already available inputs.

Unscored Theorem D (proof.md Section 9.5). In the full-cube fair representation of a d-affine disperser for a nonnegative integer d, suppose t disjoint closed blocks use jointly independent input-coordinate triples a,b,c and the nine charged objects x=a+b, y=b+c, z=c+a; P_1=a*y, P_2=b*z, P_3=(c+1)*(x+1); H_1=P_1+x, H_2=P_2+y, H_3=P_3+z, all over F_2. Block parameters and auxiliaries have no computational occurrences outside their block and cannot supply the designated output, and the only permitted external uses of internal gates are arbitrary ordinary/output uses of H_1,H_2,H_3. Then S>=4N+3t-9*(d+1); in particular N=3t gives the conditional architecture bound S>=5N-9*(d+1). No assertion says arbitrary circuits contain such blocks, and this is not a coefficient-five declaration for the challenge family.
